extracted.intended_audience: publishers, authors, and agents considering entering a short story collection in The Story Prize (also useful to readers/researchers of literary awards)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and selection practices for entering and evaluating short story collections for The Story Prize — an annual U.S. literary award honoring outstanding collections of short fiction. Covers eligibility, who may submit, judging composition, finalists and award details, and a separate Spotlight Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — language and first U.S. publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible books must be written in English and first published in the United States during a calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The collection's first U.S. publication must occur within the eligibility calendar year; translations or books first published elsewhere would not meet this criterion unless first published in the U.S. in that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may enter (submitters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers, authors, or agents may enter a short story collection written in English by a living author and published in the U.S. during a calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are accepted from publishers, the author themself, or the author's agent; the author must be living at time of entry. Entry is limited to short story collections meeting the publication/time/language criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target work type — short story collections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Story Prize honors the author of an outstanding collection of short fiction with a cash award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is explicitly for collections of short fiction (not novels, single short stories, or other forms). 'Outstanding' is the qualitative standard the judges apply when selecting finalists and the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of finalists — Director and Founder responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director and Founder together choose the three finalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the full pool of entries (typically 100–120 per year), the Director and Founder select three books to be finalists; those finalists are later presented to the independent judges who choose the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging — three independent judges and panel composition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Three independent judges choose the winner from among the three finalists; the judging group has a different composition every year and consists of a mix of writers, booksellers, readers, critics, teachers, publishers, and editors. One judge is always a fiction writer, a second judge is either a bookseller or librarian in alternating years, and the third is generally a critic or editor or someone else associated with the short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges vary yearly to provide diverse perspectives; specific composition rules require a fiction writer always on the panel and alternate the bookseller/librarian role. This composition is part of the award's evaluative procedure rather than a numerical scoring rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and public presentation of finalists/winner
rubrics_metrics.description: Three finalists are announced in January. These authors participate in an award event, typically in March, at which they read from their work and have an on-stage discussion with Dark. At the end of the event, Julie Lindsey announces the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalist announcement and the live (or recorded) award event are part of the selection/presentation process; entrants should expect public readings and discussion and that the winner will be announced at the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize amounts and winner recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Story Prize honors the author of an outstanding collection of short fiction with a $20,000 cash award. Each of two runners-up receives $5,000. The winner also receives an engraved silver bowl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary awards are awarded to the winner and two runners-up; the winner receives an additional physical prize (engraved silver bowl).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Story Prize Spotlight Award — Director-selected special recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: This $1,000 award is given to a short story collection of exceptional merit, as selected by the Director of the Story Prize, from among all entrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spotlight Award recipients might be promising works by first-time authors, collections in alternative formats, or works that demonstrate an unusual perspective on the writers’ craft — the Director has discretion to highlight atypical or emerging work that demonstrates 'exceptional merit.'
